correctness.rationale: For each spoke the closed edge neighbourhood has k spokes plus optional second edge; with two colours its unique-colour condition gives R in {0,1,k-1,k}, and forces second colours. Every internal path-edge neighbourhood of three edges must be nonmonochromatic and terminal pair must differ; backward tail recursion A_{L+1}=B_L, B_{L+1}=A_L+B_L with A2=0,B2=1 yields u/v Fibonacci values. Counting the disjoint spoke cases yields the formula, including length-one arms. Exactly two length-two u-factors vanish under the length-one prohibition, yielding zero binary counts. A tree levels-mod3 colouring provides the three-colour bound, and center degree>=3 blocks one colour. Independently built actual graph neighbourhoods and exhaustively enumerated 1,563 length profiles at small sizes; no exceptions.
residual_risks: Small finite enumeration alone cannot prove all arm lengths; k>=3 and named colours matter.

value.rationale: Spider trees are a canonical branching tree family and conflict-free edge colourability is an active natural graph invariant. The exact Fibonacci enumeration and sharp length1-plus-two-length2 obstruction provide both a complete labelled counting answer and a clean feasibility boundary; not merely a routine chromatic upper bound.
residual_risks: No generalization to arbitrary trees, proper colourings, or automorphism-quotiented counts.

final_claim: For every spider with k>=3 arms of lengths ell_i>=1 and named red/blue edge colours, the number of conflict-free edge-colourings is 2 sum_j v_j prod_{i!=j}u_i + 2 1_{all ell>=2} prod_i v_i, u_i=1 at length1 else F_{ell_i-2}, v_i=1 at length1 else F_{ell_i-1}; the minimum full conflict-free edge chromatic number is 3 iff a length1 arm and at least two length2 arms exist, otherwise 2.
limitations: Only named two-colour edge assignments are enumerated; length-one arms have no second edge and need special handling.
A prior disguised binary transfer enumeration is a residual priority risk.
